guides.title: Housing and renting in the Netherlands
guides.summary: A national starting point for renting, contracts, deposits, tenant rights, housing benefit and local housing support.

sections.what: Rental rules and routes differ for social, mid-price and private-sector housing. Start with the national rules, then check the municipality and the exact contract before acting.
sections.who: Use this route if you are looking for a room or home, checking a tenancy agreement, dealing with maintenance or service costs, or checking whether an allowance may apply.
steps: Identify whether the offer is a room, self-contained home, social, mid-price or private-sector rental.
Read the complete tenancy agreement and verify the landlord or agent before transferring money.
Check whether registration at the address is possible and which municipality handles the address.
Use the national tenant guidance and Huurcommissie route for rent, maintenance or service-cost questions.
Check the municipality for local permits, housing teams and local support.
documents: The exact documents depend on the provider and your situation. Keep the proposed contract, written offer, payment evidence and relevant correspondence; verify any additional request with the responsible official source.
sections.cost: YouNew does not reproduce changing rent limits, fees or allowance amounts. Check the dated official source before making a financial decision.
sections.timing: Waiting times and application periods differ by housing route and municipality. The responsible provider or authority is the source for current timing.
problems: For a dispute about rent, maintenance or service costs, use the Huurcommissie guidance to check whether it can handle the case.
For suspected fraud or pressure to pay before verification, stop and verify the provider and contract independently.
For local registration or permit questions, contact the municipality for the address.
mistakes: Treating every rental as governed by the same rules.
Paying before verifying the home, provider and written terms.
Assuming an address can be registered without checking.
sections.localDifferences: Selecting a city keeps this national guidance visible and adds verified province, municipality and local results when they exist. It never invents local services.

guides.title: Work and employment in the Netherlands
guides.summary: A national route for finding work and checking contracts, pay, working conditions, sick leave, dismissal and UWV services.

sections.what: Dutch employment rules cover contracts, pay, working time, leave, illness, working conditions and ending employment. The applicable route depends on your contract and status.
sections.who: Use this route when looking for a job, reviewing an offer or contract, checking pay or leave, reporting unsafe work, or dealing with unemployment or dismissal.
steps: Identify whether the role is direct employment, agency work, self-employment or another contract form.
Keep the written offer and contract and check the employer, hours, pay components and applicable collective agreement.
Use official Government.nl guidance for employment rules and Werk.nl or UWV for the relevant work or unemployment service.
Use an official labour or legal-help route when terms are unclear or a problem cannot be resolved.
documents: Requirements depend on the employer and legal route. Keep the contract, payslips, work schedule and relevant correspondence; verify identity or residence-document requests with the responsible authority.
sections.cost: YouNew does not reproduce changing salary thresholds, benefit amounts or service fees. Use the current official calculation or decision.
sections.timing: Application, notice and objection periods depend on the specific process. Check the official page or decision immediately rather than relying on a generic deadline.
problems: For unemployment or work-service questions, use UWV or Werk.nl.
For unsafe or unfair working conditions, use the official labour-inspection or legal-help route appropriate to the issue.
mistakes: Starting without understanding the contract form.
Relying on verbal promises that are absent from the written terms.
Using an outdated wage or notice-period figure.
sections.localDifferences: Most employment rules are national. City selection adds verified local job services when available but cannot hide this national route.

guides.title: BSN, registration, DigiD and residence documents
guides.summary: A national route that separates municipal registration and BSN, DigiD, address changes and IND residence documents.

sections.what: BSN, BRP registration, DigiD and residence documents are related but different. Municipalities handle local registration routes, DigiD is the government login service, and IND handles residence applications and documents.
sections.who: Use this route when you need a BSN, need to register or change an address, need DigiD, or need the correct IND residence-document route.
steps: Choose the exact task: BSN, municipality registration, DigiD, address change or an IND residence matter.
For registration, open the official municipality page for the address and check its current appointment and document list.
Use the official DigiD site for application, activation and recovery.
Use IND for residence-permit and residence-document procedures.
Do not send identity documents through an unofficial form or contact route.
documents: The required documents depend on the task and personal situation. Use the official municipality, DigiD or IND checklist for the exact application.
sections.cost: Fees depend on the procedure and can change. Use the current official page or formal decision.
sections.timing: Appointment availability and decision periods differ. The responsible municipality, DigiD or IND page is authoritative for current timing.
problems: If a municipality route is unclear, use its official contact page.
For DigiD access problems, use DigiD support without sharing login credentials.
For a residence case, use the IND route that matches the permit or document.
mistakes: Treating DigiD as a BSN application.
Using the wrong municipality for an address.
Uploading identity documents to an unverified website.
sections.localDifferences: Municipal registration and appointments are local. The national explanation and official national services remain available for every selected city.

guides.title: Healthcare, huisarts and health insurance
guides.summary: A national starting point for huisarts care, hospitals, pharmacies, dentists, urgent care and Dutch health insurance.

sections.what: Dutch healthcare uses different routes for routine primary care, urgent care, hospital care and emergencies. Insurance questions are separate from finding the right care route.
sections.who: Use this route to find a huisarts, understand which care route to use, locate a hospital or pharmacy, or check official health-insurance information.
steps: For immediate life-threatening danger, use the emergency route and call 112.
For non-emergency care, identify whether you need routine huisarts care, urgent out-of-hours care, dental care, a pharmacy or another service.
Use the official health-insurance guidance for coverage obligations and choices.
Use verified local results or the municipality and insurer directories; call the provider to confirm availability.
documents: A provider or insurer may require identification, insurance details or a referral depending on the service. Confirm the exact requirement with that provider.
sections.cost: Coverage and personal costs depend on the service and policy. Verify them with the insurer and provider before non-emergency treatment when possible.
sections.timing: Availability varies by provider and urgency. Do not delay emergency care while checking a directory.
problems: If you cannot find a local huisarts accepting patients, ask your insurer for its current care-finding route.
For urgent but non-life-threatening problems outside normal hours, use the local official out-of-hours route.
mistakes: Using an emergency route for routine administration.
Assuming every provider has the same availability or insurance contract.
Treating a directory entry as confirmation that new patients are accepted.
sections.localDifferences: Provider availability is local and changes. YouNew shows only verified local entries and keeps national healthcare guidance visible.

guides.title: Education and learning Dutch
guides.summary: A national route for schools, MBO, HBO, university, adult learning, Dutch courses, NT2, Taalhuis and diploma questions.

sections.what: Education routes include school, MBO, HBO, university, adult learning and Dutch-language learning. Admission, fees and finance depend on the programme and personal situation.
sections.who: Use this route when choosing an education level, looking for Dutch lessons, checking DUO services, or finding the responsible route for a diploma.
steps: Choose the goal: compulsory school, vocational or higher education, adult learning, Dutch language or diploma recognition.
Use the official education overview and the institution's own admission information.
Use DUO for the relevant registration, finance, exam or diploma service.
For local Dutch practice and Taalhuis activities, check the municipality or public library and verify the current programme.
documents: Admission and finance documents depend on the institution, level, nationality and situation. Use the exact institution and DUO checklist.
sections.cost: Course fees, tuition and finance amounts change. YouNew links to the authoritative provider instead of storing an amount.
sections.timing: Application and enrolment periods differ by programme. Check them before relying on a general academic calendar.
problems: Contact the institution for admission or enrolment issues.
Use DUO for its official service or decision.
For local language support, check a verified municipality or library route.
mistakes: Assuming every Dutch course is an approved civic-integration school.
Missing an institution-specific application period.
Using an unofficial diploma or finance service.
sections.localDifferences: Schools, courses, libraries and Taalhuis activities are local. National education and DUO guidance remains visible for every city.

guides.title: SIM cards, phone contracts and internet
guides.summary: A national consumer route for prepaid SIM, eSIM, mobile contracts, internet services, switching and provider complaints.

sections.what: Mobile and internet offers differ by provider, contract form, coverage and identity checks. ACM ConsuWijzer publishes independent consumer guidance in Dutch.
sections.who: Use this route when choosing prepaid or a contract, comparing eSIM or physical SIM options, arranging internet, switching or handling a provider complaint.
steps: Choose prepaid or a contract and check whether the device supports the required SIM type.
Compare the complete contract, duration, cancellation and coverage information directly with providers.
Verify identity and payment requests on the provider's official domain.
Use ACM ConsuWijzer for independent consumer guidance and complaints routes.
documents: Provider requirements differ. Confirm identification, address and payment requirements directly with the provider before starting an order.
sections.cost: Plans and promotions change frequently. YouNew does not rank providers or reproduce prices.
sections.timing: Activation and installation times are provider-specific. Check the order confirmation and provider status.
problems: Contact the provider first for activation, billing or cancellation issues.
Use the independent ACM consumer route if the problem is not resolved.
mistakes: Choosing only by a temporary headline price.
Ignoring contract duration or cancellation terms.
Sending identity documents to an unverified seller.
sections.localDifferences: Coverage and fixed-network availability depend on the exact address. YouNew does not request or store a precise address.

guides.title: Rules, traffic and fines in the Netherlands
guides.summary: A national route for traffic and bicycle rules, CJIB letters and fines, with municipality links for parking, waste, noise and local rules.

sections.what: National traffic enforcement and CJIB correspondence are different from municipality parking, waste, noise and other local rules. Start with the issuer shown on the official notice.
sections.who: Use this route when checking a traffic or parking fine, road or bicycle rules, a CJIB letter, or a municipality rule.
steps: Read the notice and identify the issuer, reference and official response route.
For a CJIB notice, use the official CJIB website typed or opened independently.
For municipality parking, waste or noise matters, use the selected municipality's official website.
Check the official decision for the applicable payment, objection or appeal route and date.
documents: Keep the original notice, reference, date and any evidence. The official notice states the exact information required for payment or challenge.
sections.cost: YouNew does not reproduce fine amounts or payment details. Use only the official notice and official authority website.
sections.timing: Deadlines are case-specific and legally important. Follow the date and route on the official notice immediately.
problems: If a payment request looks suspicious, do not use its link; navigate independently to the named authority.
Use the formal objection or appeal information in the decision rather than a generic contact form.
mistakes: Assuming every parking fine is issued by the same authority.
Paying through an unverified message or QR code.
Missing a case-specific deadline while searching for general information.
sections.localDifferences: Parking, waste, noise and pet rules can be municipal. City selection adds the verified municipality site and never removes national CJIB or traffic guidance.

guides.title: LGBTIQ+ support and discrimination help
guides.summary: A safe national starting point for LGBTIQ+ community support, discrimination advice, reporting an incident and urgent danger in the Netherlands.

sections.what: Different routes apply to community support, discrimination advice, a formal report and immediate danger. YouNew keeps those routes separate and links to the responsible national service.
sections.who: Use this route if you want a confidential LGBTIQ+ support contact, have experienced discrimination or intimidation, want to understand reporting options, or need a safer next step.
steps: If there is immediate danger or violence is happening now, call 112. Do not wait for an online directory or form.
For a confidential conversation about sexual orientation or gender identity, open the current COC Switchboard contact options.
For discrimination advice or a report, use Discriminatie.nl and choose whether you want follow-up contact or an anonymous report.
For legal context and other complaint routes, read the current Government.nl guidance on reporting discrimination.
For community activities or a local contact, use COC Nederland's regional network and confirm the current details with the organization.
documents: Support conversations generally do not require a YouNew account. For a report, keep relevant dates, messages, screenshots or other evidence, but follow the chosen service's current form and privacy guidance.
sections.cost: YouNew does not charge for this guidance. Check the responsible service for its current contact conditions; never pay an unverified intermediary to file a discrimination report.
sections.timing: Response times and opening hours can change. Open the responsible source for current availability; use 112 immediately when there is urgent danger.
problems: If one support channel is closed, use the provider's listed alternative contact method or another responsible source on this page.
If an incident may be criminal or there is a continuing safety risk, use the police or emergency route appropriate to the urgency.
For discrimination by an employer, landlord, school or service provider, keep written evidence and check the formal complaint route as well as independent advice.
mistakes: Using a community support line as an emergency service.
Publishing sensitive personal information in a public review or social-media post before considering privacy and safety.
Assuming a national directory confirms a local organization's current opening hours.
sections.localDifferences: Local community activities and discrimination services differ by region. City selection may add verified local options, while this national route remains visible everywhere in the Netherlands.

officialSources.title: Combating discrimination and violence against LGBTIQ+ people

guides.title: Bank accounts and everyday payments
guides.summary: A neutral route for choosing a regulated payment provider, preparing a personal bank-account application, understanding Dutch payment options and handling a rejected application.

sections.what: Banks and other payment providers set their own acceptance process, documents, account features and fees within Dutch and European rules. YouNew does not rank providers or accept account applications.
sections.who: Use this route when opening a personal payment account, checking whether a provider is regulated, comparing account conditions or looking for the responsible route after a rejection.
steps: Decide whether you need a personal payment account or a separate business account.
Compare the complete conditions, identification process, fees and support language on each provider's official website.
Check the provider in the current DNB public register before sending identity documents or money.
Prepare only the documents requested by the selected provider and submit them through its verified application route.
If a regular account is refused, read the official basic-payment-account guidance and the provider's written reason before choosing the next route.
documents: Requirements vary by provider and situation. A provider may ask for valid identification, contact details, residence information, a BSN or tax-residency information; use its current checklist rather than a generic list.
sections.cost: Account fees and payment charges change. YouNew does not reproduce prices or recommend a commercial provider.
sections.timing: Application and verification times are provider-specific. A complete application can still require additional checks.
problems: Ask the provider for its complaint or review route when an application is delayed or refused.
Use the basic payment account information when the ordinary route is unavailable and the stated conditions may apply.
Stop if a message asks for login codes, remote access or payment to release an account.
mistakes: Choosing an account from an advertisement without checking the regulated provider.
Sending identity documents through email or messaging when the provider has a secure route.
Assuming every applicant must provide exactly the same documents.
sections.localDifferences: Bank accounts are national services. Branch availability and in-person support can differ by city, but a city filter must not hide this national route.

guides.title: Family, childcare and school basics
guides.summary: A national starting point for childcare, after-school care, childcare benefit and the responsible school or municipality route for families with children.

sections.what: Childcare, after-school care, school registration and family support are separate routes. Availability is local, while benefit conditions and education rules are national.
sections.who: Use this route when looking for childcare or BSO, checking childcare benefit, arranging school for a child or finding the responsible local family service.
steps: Choose the exact need: childcare, BSO, primary school, benefit or family support.
For childcare, verify the provider, current availability and contract directly before signing.
Check the current childcare-benefit conditions before relying on an estimated contribution.
For school admission, use the municipality and the school's official procedure for your address and the child's age.
Report relevant changes promptly through the responsible official service.
documents: Requirements depend on the service. Use the provider, school, municipality or Dienst Toeslagen checklist for identification, registration, income and contract information.
sections.cost: Childcare prices and benefit calculations change. Use the provider contract and current official calculation; YouNew does not store amounts.
sections.timing: Waiting lists, school admission dates and benefit application periods differ. Check them before committing to a start date.
problems: Ask the municipality about local family support when regular childcare or school routes do not fit the situation.
Contact Dienst Toeslagen for an official benefit decision or correction.
Use the provider's complaints route for contract or service issues.
mistakes: Treating childcare registration and childcare benefit as one application.
Assuming a provider has a place because it appears in a directory.
Using an old benefit estimate after income, hours or household circumstances change.
sections.localDifferences: Childcare capacity, school admission procedures and family teams are local. City selection adds verified local routes while keeping national benefit guidance visible.

guides.title: Pets, dogs and cats in the Netherlands
guides.summary: A national route for pet welfare rules, dog microchipping and registration, importing an animal, local dog tax and finding the responsible veterinarian or authority.

sections.what: Rules differ by animal and situation. Dog identification and registration, importing an animal, welfare duties and municipality dog rules must be checked separately.
sections.who: Use this route when buying, adopting, bringing or keeping a pet, registering a dog, checking a pet passport or finding the correct local rule.
steps: Identify the animal and whether it is already in the Netherlands, being imported, bought or adopted.
For a dog, check the current microchip, registration and passport route before a transfer or import.
For travel or import, use the responsible NVWA or RVO route for the country and animal.
Confirm local dog tax, leash, waste and restricted-area rules with the municipality.
Use a veterinarian for animal-health advice and for procedures that require an authorised professional.
documents: The required records depend on the animal and route. They may include a microchip record, pet passport, animal health certificate, ownership or import information; use the official checklist.
sections.cost: Veterinary, registration and municipality charges differ. Verify current costs with the responsible provider or authority.
sections.timing: Registration and import actions can have strict situation-specific periods. Check the current official page before travel, purchase or adoption.
problems: Contact a veterinarian or the responsible authority if the chip, passport or ownership record is missing or inconsistent.
Use the municipality for a removed animal, local nuisance rule or dog-tax question.
Do not transport an animal when the official import conditions have not been confirmed.
mistakes: Assuming dogs and cats have identical registration rules.
Buying an animal without checking the chip, registration and seller information.
Relying on a municipality rule from a different city.
sections.localDifferences: Dog tax, leash areas, waste rules and local animal services differ by municipality. National welfare and registration guidance remains visible for every city.

guides.title: Taxes and income tax returns
guides.summary: A national route for understanding a Dutch tax letter, preparing an income tax return, distinguishing resident and non-resident routes and using Mijn Belastingdienst safely.

sections.what: The correct tax route depends on where you live, the income involved, whether you received an invitation and whether you moved across a border during the tax year.
sections.who: Use this route when you receive a Belastingdienst letter, need to prepare an income tax return, moved into or out of the Netherlands, or have Dutch and foreign income.
steps: Read the complete official letter and identify the tax type, year, deadline and response route.
Choose the resident, non-resident or migration-year route that matches the official guidance.
Prepare your DigiD or accepted login and the records listed for the selected return.
Check pre-filled information against your own annual statements and records before submitting.
Save the official confirmation and use the formal objection or payment route shown on the decision when needed.
documents: Documents depend on the return. Use the current Belastingdienst preparation list and keep the official letter, annual statements, relevant account and housing records, and information about foreign income when applicable.
sections.cost: YouNew does not calculate tax or reproduce thresholds. Use the official return and assessment, or an authorised adviser for personal advice.
sections.timing: Deadlines depend on the letter, tax year and return type. Follow the official date rather than a general calendar reminder.
problems: Use the official appointment or help route if you cannot complete the return.
Request formal clarification or use the objection route stated on an assessment when you disagree.
Verify payment details independently on the official Belastingdienst domain before paying.
mistakes: Using the non-resident return only because some income came from abroad.
Submitting without checking pre-filled data.
Paying through an account number copied from an unverified message.
sections.localDifferences: Income tax is national. Municipal taxes are separate and must be checked with the municipality or regional tax authority named on the notice.

officialSources.title: Filing an online tax return in four steps

guides.title: Benefits and allowances
guides.summary: A national starting point for healthcare, rent, childcare and supplementary child benefits, with safe checks for eligibility, changes and Mijn toeslagen.

sections.what: Dutch allowances are separate schemes with different conditions. Entitlement can depend on residence status, household, income, assets, insurance, housing or registered childcare.
sections.who: Use this route when checking healthcare, rent, childcare or supplementary child benefit, applying through Mijn toeslagen or reporting a change.
steps: Choose the exact allowance and read its current conditions before applying.
Check which people, income, assets, residence status, contract or insurance information the scheme uses.
Use Mijn toeslagen or the listed official help route and keep the confirmation.
Review the decision and estimated information against your actual situation.
Report relevant changes promptly and stop or adjust a benefit when the official guidance requires it.
documents: Requirements depend on the allowance. You may need BSNs, DigiD, income estimates, housing or childcare contract information and insurance details; follow the current official checklist.
sections.cost: Applying through the official service does not require a commercial intermediary. YouNew does not calculate eligibility or amounts.
sections.timing: Application periods and change-reporting duties differ by allowance. Check the dated official page and decision immediately.
problems: Use the official help or appointment route if Mijn toeslagen is not accessible or the Dutch-language process is unclear.
Correct an estimate when circumstances change to reduce the risk of repayment.
Use the formal decision route when you disagree with an outcome.
mistakes: Treating all allowances as one combined benefit.
Using an old income estimate after work or household changes.
Assuming nationality alone decides eligibility.
sections.localDifferences: National allowances are handled by Dienst Toeslagen. Separate municipality income support and local schemes can differ and should be checked locally.

officialSources.title: I want to apply for a benefit

guides.title: Public transport, bicycles and safe travel
guides.summary: A national route for planning public transport, checking in and out, buying a bicycle safely, cycling rules and what to do if a bicycle is stolen or removed.

sections.what: Public transport and cycling use different providers and rules. Current travel information, check-in methods, bicycle safety and local parking or removal rules must be verified separately.
sections.who: Use this route when planning a journey, choosing a check-in method, buying a new or used bicycle, learning cycling basics or dealing with a missing bicycle.
steps: Plan the journey shortly before departure with the responsible operator or travel planner.
Use one supported payment or travel card consistently to check in and out and review the provider's correction route for mistakes.
Before buying a used bicycle, record the seller, receipt and frame or chip number and check the official stolen-bicycle route.
Read the current cycling and bicycle-light rules before riding.
If a bicycle is missing, first check the municipality bicycle depot and then use the official theft-reporting route when appropriate.
documents: For public transport, keep the travel or payment reference for a correction. For a bicycle, keep the receipt, frame or chip number, brand, model, colour and photographs.
sections.cost: Fares, subscriptions and bicycle prices change. Use the responsible operator or seller for current costs and terms.
sections.timing: Timetables and disruptions change in real time. Theft reporting and municipality depot retention periods can also be time-sensitive.
problems: Use the operator's correction route for a missed check-in or check-out.
Check whether the municipality removed the bicycle before reporting theft.
Do not ride an electric bicycle that does not meet the applicable vehicle rules.
mistakes: Using different contactless cards for check-in and check-out.
Buying a used bicycle without recording the frame number and seller.
Assuming bicycle parking rules are identical in every city.
sections.localDifferences: Operators, parking zones, bicycle depots and removal rules differ by city. National travel and safety guidance remains visible with local results.

officialSources.title: Check whether a bicycle is registered as stolen

guides.title: Immigration, visas and residence permits
guides.summary: A national route for identifying the responsible IND procedure for short stay, MVV, work, study, family, asylum, extension or permanent residence without mixing it with municipal registration.

sections.what: Immigration procedures depend on nationality, length and purpose of stay, sponsor and current residence status. IND procedures are separate from BRP registration and receiving a BSN from a municipality.
sections.who: Use this route to identify the correct IND procedure for entry, work, study, family, asylum, extension, replacement, permanent residence or citizenship.
steps: Identify nationality, current country and intended purpose and duration of stay.
Use the IND navigation route to choose the exact residence purpose before collecting documents or paying a fee.
Confirm whether an MVV, sponsor or recognised sponsor is part of the selected procedure.
Use only the current IND checklist, fee page and application route for that procedure.
After arrival, handle municipality registration, BSN, DigiD and health insurance as separate tasks where applicable.
documents: Requirements are procedure-specific. Use the selected IND checklist for passports, civil-status documents, sponsor evidence, income evidence, legalisation, translation and biometrics.
sections.cost: Fees and exemptions change by procedure and applicant. Use the current IND fee page before payment.
sections.timing: Decision periods, appointment availability and document validity differ. Follow the current procedure and formal correspondence.
problems: Check My IND or the official status route for a submitted application.
Use the IND replacement route for a lost or stolen residence document.
Seek qualified legal help for an adverse decision or case-specific legal question rather than relying on a general guide.
mistakes: Applying under the wrong residence purpose.
Treating municipal registration as a residence-permit application.
Using an unofficial intermediary or sending identity documents outside the official route.
sections.localDifferences: IND procedures are national. Municipality registration and local newcomer services differ by address and follow after or alongside the applicable immigration route.
